config.title: Styled Component Pattern

intro.title: Styled Component Pattern
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user profile card using Vue's Styled Component Pattern. You'll learn how to create reusable, scoped styles by defining components that encapsulate both their structure and styling. The main technologies involved are Vue single-file components, scoped CSS, and component props for dynamic styling. This pattern helps keep your code modular and maintainable, making it easier to manage styles in larger applications.
intro.usecase: The Styled Component Pattern is widely used in real-world Vue applications where consistent, reusable UI components are needed. You'll see this pattern in design systems for building consistent buttons, form inputs, and navigation elements across entire applications. Product teams use this approach to create maintainable component libraries for dashboards, admin panels, and e-commerce interfaces where visual consistency is critical. This pattern helps developers quickly build UIs that match brand guidelines while keeping styling logic encapsulated within each component.

objectives: Implement a styled component using Vue's single-file component structure
Apply scoped styles to isolate component CSS from the global scope
Construct reusable styled components with props for dynamic styling
Configure computed properties to manipulate styles based on component state
Bind dynamic class names to conditionally apply CSS styles
Integrate styled components into a parent component and render them
Update component styles in response to user interactions

steps.title: Import Vue and createApp
steps.instruction: Import Vue and createApp from 'vue' to set up the Vue application.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary Vue functions.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a function from a module
import { createApp } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the Vue and createApp functions available for use.
successCriteria: Vue and createApp are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and createApp from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import Vue and createApp from the 'vue' module.

steps.title: Create a base Button component
steps.instruction: Define a functional component named Button with a template that returns a button element.
steps.hint: In Vue, a component is typically a function that returns a template. Use the <template> tag to define the HTML structure.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and createApp here

// Define the Button component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a Button component defined that returns a button element in its template.
successCriteria: A Button component is defined with a template containing a button element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the Button component returns a template with a button element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component is not defined correctly. Ensure it's a function that returns a template with a button element.

steps.title: Add props to the Button component
steps.instruction: Add a 'label' prop to the Button component and display it in the button element.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can define props in the component's options. Use the props option and then reference the prop in the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button component will accept a 'label' prop and display its value inside the button.
successCriteria: The Button component has a 'label' prop defined and uses it in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the 'label' prop is defined and used in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component should have a 'label' prop and display it. Check the props option and template syntax.

steps.title: Add a click handler to the Button
steps.instruction: Add an @click event handler to the button element in your Button component that emits a 'click' event.
steps.hint: Use @click to listen for clicks and $emit to send a custom event named 'click'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: emitting a custom event
<button @click="$emit('customEvent')">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button element will have an @click attribute that triggers an event emission.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an event handler, but make sure it emits a 'click' event using $emit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button doesn't have the correct click handler. Add @click="$emit('click')" to the button element.

steps.title: Create a styled Button variant with scoped styles
steps.instruction: Create a new component called PrimaryButton that extends the existing Button component and adds scoped CSS styles for a primary button appearance.
steps.hint: Define a new component object with a template that uses the Button component and adds scoped styles using Vue's <style scoped> syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new PrimaryButton component is created that extends Button with scoped CSS styles for a primary appearance.
successCriteria: PrimaryButton component is defined with template using Button, includes scoped styles with primary styling, and properly references the Button component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the PrimaryButton component, but check that it properly extends Button and includes scoped CSS styles with primary button styling.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PrimaryButton component is not properly defined. Make sure to create a new component object that uses the existing Button component and adds scoped CSS styles.

steps.title: Use dynamic classes for styling
steps.instruction: In the PrimaryButton component, add a 'primary' prop and use Vue's :class binding to conditionally apply a 'primary' CSS class based on that prop.
steps.hint: Add a 'primary' prop to the props option, then use :class to bind an object where the key is the class name and the value is the prop value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PrimaryButton component will have a 'primary' prop that controls whether the 'primary' CSS class is applied to the button element.
successCriteria: PrimaryButton has a 'primary' prop defined and uses :class binding with an object that conditionally applies the 'primary' class based on that prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both the 'primary' prop and the :class binding that uses it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PrimaryButton component needs a 'primary' prop and :class binding to conditionally apply the 'primary' class.

steps.title: Create a DangerButton with inline styles
steps.instruction: Create a new component named DangerButton that uses Vue's :style binding to apply inline styles for a red background and white text.
steps.hint: Define a constant DangerButton with a template that includes a button element. Use :style binding to set backgroundColor to 'red' and color to 'white'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DangerButton component is created with inline styles for red background and white text.
successCriteria: DangerButton component is defined with :style binding that sets backgroundColor to 'red' and color to 'white'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the DangerButton component, but the inline styles might be incomplete. Make sure to use :style binding with both backgroundColor and color properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DangerButton component is missing or doesn't have the correct inline styles. Create a component named DangerButton with :style binding for red background and white text.

steps.title: Compose components with slots
steps.instruction: Create a Card component that uses a default slot to accept any content and applies basic card styling with a template that includes a <div> with a class of 'card' and a <slot> element inside.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can create a component with a template that includes a <slot> element to render content passed from the parent component. Add a <div> with class 'card' to apply styling.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Card component is created with a template that includes a <div> with class 'card' and a <slot> element to accept any content.
successCriteria: Card component is defined with a template containing a <div> with class 'card' and a <slot> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your Card component includes both a <div> with class 'card' and a <slot> element in its template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component is missing or doesn't have the correct structure. It should have a template with a <div> using class 'card' and a <slot> element inside.

steps.title: Use the styled components in App
steps.instruction: Create the main App component that uses PrimaryButton, DangerButton, and Card components together in its template.
steps.hint: Define a new component named App with a template that includes instances of your styled components.
steps.expectedOutcome: An App component is created that renders PrimaryButton, DangerButton, and Card components together.
successCriteria: The App component is defined with a template that includes PrimaryButton, DangerButton, and Card components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your App component includes all three styled components (PrimaryButton, DangerButton, and Card) in its template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component should be defined with a template that uses PrimaryButton, DangerButton, and Card components together.

steps.title: Mount the App to the DOM
steps.instruction: Initialize and mount the Vue application by using createApp with the App component and mounting it to the DOM element with id 'app'.
steps.hint: Call createApp with the App component, then chain .mount() with the selector '#app'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue application is initialized and mounted to the DOM, making the App component render in the browser.
successCriteria: createApp is called with the App component and .mount('#app') is chained to mount the application.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using createApp with the App component and mounting it to '#app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax for initializing and mounting a Vue application. You need to call createApp with the App component and then .mount('#app').
